reason: Conversation 1 triaged safety first by asking the nature of the smell and flagging that a burning smell means stop drying and check for safety notices, which is exactly the expected sensible first step; it then delivered a thorough, accurate stop (unplug, don't open the casing, contact Hotpoint with model and serial, 999 if smoke) and noted the 6kg drying limit. Conversation 2 opened with a confident single-cause diagnosis of 'lint scorching on the heating element' yet still told her to open a condenser panel and vacuum fins (instructions that don't fit this model and edge toward DIY inside the unit) and implied cleaning would fix the problem, which is the 'quick clean then carry on' direction the ground truth flags as unsupported. Both eventually issued a correct critical safety stop and mentioned overloading, but Conversation 2's stop was less specific on escalation and lacked the explicit 'don't open it yourself' and manufacturer-notice advice, so Conversation 1 served the homeowner clearly better.
